assessment: This study presents a valuable finding that rTMS over the aPFC, applied before threat memory retrieval, can immediately decrease implicit reactions to learned and novel stimuli in humans and that these effects can persist one week later, in the absence of rTMS. The evidence supporting the claims of the authors is solid and raise important hypotheses for further research. The work will be of interest to researchers in the fields of neuromodulation and affective neuroscience.
